dev.$comment_requiredCorsOrigins: FORCING FUNCTION (spaarke-auth-v4-dataverse-MI task 090, 2026-08-25). Every origin listed here MUST be present in the target App Service's Cors__AllowedOrigins__N settings; Deploy-BffApi.ps1 asserts it after each deploy and FAILS if one is missing. WHY THIS EXISTS: commit 66a45cf6a removed the blanket credentialed *.azurestaticapps.net CORS rule (correct — it is an attacker-registrable shared domain) and its commit message named a DEPLOYMENT PREREQ to enumerate our SWA origins explicitly. Nobody ran it, nothing failed, and the gap surfaced only when a human opened the Outlook add-in during UAT. WHAT TO LIST: ONLY origins that CorsModule's suffix rules do NOT already cover — i.e. NOT *.dynamics.com, *.powerapps.com or *.powerappsportals.com, which are matched in code. Listing covered origins adds noise without adding protection. WHAT THE CHECK IS: 'every declared origin is present', NOT 'live equals declared' — environments legitimately carry extra origins, and an exact-match check would fail on every deploy and be disabled within a month.

_template.$comment_requiredCorsOrigins: REQUIRED (may be empty). Origins that MUST appear in this environment's Cors__AllowedOrigins__N App Settings. List ONLY origins CorsModule's suffix rules do not already match — so NOT *.dynamics.com / *.powerapps.com / *.powerappsportals.com. In practice this means your Azure Static Web App front-ends (Office add-ins, external SPA). Deploy-BffApi.ps1 asserts these after every deploy and fails if one is missing. Leaving the key ABSENT makes the deploy warn that the environment is unaudited; an explicit empty array asserts 'this environment genuinely has no SWA front-ends'.
